tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Asteroids, Comets & Meteoroids

questions.question: Q: Why do comet tails always point away from the Sun?
questions.correctAnswer: The solar wind and radiation pressure push ionised gas and dust away from the Sun, so tails always point away regardless of the comet's direction of travel.

questions.question: Q: Distinguish between a meteor and a meteorite.
questions.correctAnswer: A meteor is the visible streak of light produced when a meteoroid enters and burns up in the atmosphere. A meteorite is a fragment that survives passage through the atmosphere and reaches the ground.

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between short-period and long-period comets?
questions.correctAnswer: Short-period comets have orbital periods under 200 years and originate from the Kuiper belt. Long-period comets have periods over 200 years and originate from the Oort cloud.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Asteroids, Comets & Meteoroids

questions.question: Q: Why is the asteroid belt not a destroyed planet?
questions.correctAnswer: The total mass of the asteroid belt is only about 4% of the Moon's mass — far too little to form a planet. Jupiter's gravity prevented accretion into a single body.

questions.question: Q: Describe the structure of a comet when near the Sun.
questions.correctAnswer: Near the Sun, a comet develops a coma (fuzzy envelope of gas and dust around the nucleus) and two tails: a straight ion tail of ionised gas and a curved dust tail.
